result.answer:
## Answer: Yes, you will need to pay the ¥12,000 assessment fee again

Since your March claim (the first) was approved and this new incident is only your **second** claim in a rolling 12-month period, you don't yet meet the threshold for a fee waiver.

**The rule, quoted from the site:**
> "Claimants with two or more approved claims from separate incidents within any rolling 12-month period are exempt from the ¥12,000 assessment fee."
— *Claims FAQ*, [/claims/faq/#fee-waivers](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/faq/)

The waiver requires **at least 2 prior approved claims** (making the current one your 3rd+). Right now you have only 1 approved claim (March) counted toward that threshold, so the waiver condition isn't met yet.

**What this means for you:**
- **This claim (2nd incident):** Fee of ¥12,000 is due, per the standard fee schedule — *"The claim assessment fee is ¥12,000, payable when the claim is lodged."* ([/claims/fees/](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/fees/))
- **Silver lining:** If your final award exceeds ¥1,000,000, the fee is refunded in full — *"The assessment fee is refunded in full where the final award exceeds ¥1,000,000."* ([/claims/fees/](https://office-of-kaiju-affairs.vercel.app/claims/fees/))
- **Looking ahead:** If you have a **third** approved claim from a separate incident within 12 months of the first, that third claim (and any thereafter within the rolling window) would qualify for the fee waiver.

Since your bakery is a commercial property in Zone 4 with verified structural damage, you do remain eligible for the underlying compensation itself (including business-interruption coverage) — just not exempt from this particular fee on claim #2.

normalisations: A field value counts if it CONTAINS the expected value — "Zone 4" satisfies "4".
A boolean counts if it reads as affirmative — "Yes" satisfies true.

A select counts if its visible LABEL matches the expected option value with case and punctuation collapsed — "Structural alteration" satisfies "structural-alteration". A UI agent picks the option it can read; scoring the label as a miss would measure transcription rather than comprehension.

These three were ADDED AFTER defects were found in this scorer, not designed in from the start. Each one existed because a check had already scored an answer wrongly, and the last of them changed a finding that had already been handed over. They are listed so a reader can judge the instrument, including its history.

Answer text is normalised before matching: NFKC, Unicode dashes folded to "-", non-breaking spaces to " ", curly quotes to straight, and markdown emphasis markers removed. A model that writes "rolling 12‑month" or "only **one** approved" is making the same claim as one that does not.
A conclusion is read from position, not vocabulary: a correct answer quotes the rule it applies, so waiver wording inside a quotation does not outrank an explicit finding stated earlier.
Affirmative phrases are only counted when not negated within the preceding ~28 characters, so "should not have to pay" is not read as "have to pay".
